title: Perforated Peptic Ulcer: Peritonitis and Initial Assessment
subject: Surgery
preview: Perforated peptic ulcer can present with sudden severe abdominal pain, generalized peritonitis and physiological instability.
quickRevision: Perforated peptic ulcer can present with sudden severe abdominal pain, generalized peritonitis and physiological instability.
Initial assessment addresses airway, circulation, analgesia and urgent surgical review.
NSAID exposure and Helicobacter pylori are important ulcer-related factors.

sections.title: Clinical syndrome and red flags
points: Perforated peptic ulcer can present with sudden severe abdominal pain, generalized peritonitis and physiological instability.
Free intraperitoneal air may be visible on appropriate imaging but is not invariably present.

sections.title: Differentiate and manage
points: Initial assessment addresses airway, circulation, analgesia and urgent surgical review.
NSAID exposure and Helicobacter pylori are important ulcer-related factors.

sections.title: Exam trap — avoid this mistake
points: Absence of visible free air on a plain film does not rule out perforation.
